Based on the healthcare Q&A matches provided, the comprehensive answer to the user's question about the symptoms of acid reflux (GERD) is as follows:

Acid reflux, also known as gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), is a condition where the stomach contents flow back up into the esophagus, causing symptoms such as heartburn, regurgitation of food or liquid, difficulty swallowing, chest pain, chronic cough, hoarse voice, and sensation of a lump in the throat. Symptoms often worsen when lying down or bending over.

To manage GERD symptoms, lifestyle modifications and medications may be recommended.
